own_solution.law: COP_Carnot = Tc/(Th - Tc) = 275/25 = 11; COP = 0.3 × 11 = 3.3. The compressor input is Pw = Pc/COP = 200/3.3 = 60.6061 W. An operating interior lamp adds its power q to the wall heat load, giving Pw = (200 + q)/3.3.
assumptions: The stated 200 W is the heat entering through the refrigerator walls.
The interior and kitchen remain at their stated temperatures.
The stated COP relates heat removal to compressor electrical input and applies to each added sentence.
An operating interior lamp supplies its electrical power as interior heat.
Steady operation removes dependence on thermal transients from the earlier test.

T2CD6.regime: The required compressor electrical input is below the continuous motor rating: 60.6061 W < q. All listed ratings satisfy this condition.

notes: The authors' claims agree with the locked pass-1 solution. For either relevant lamp sentence, powers of 35, 55 and 90 W give compressor inputs of 71.2121, 77.2727 and 87.8788 W, respectively. Every certified invariant answer is also correct. Test duration cancels between total work and elapsed time; converting minutes to seconds in both factors preserves this cancellation. The earlier-test lamp has no remaining effect under steady operation, and the exterior lamp does not change the prescribed kitchen reservoir temperature. Both declared minimal pairs preserve the 55 W quantity and change its temporal or spatial attachment as intended. The numeral-free sentences are explicitly identified as controls, resolving the qualification noted in pass 1.
